newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on overbought signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on overbought signals.

text.p: Commission house selling in late dealings drove CBOT wheat futures to a lower close with signals the market was overbought for the short term leading the way down, traders said.
"It was just profit taking today. The December has been on a big ride lately," said Ron Kucha of Chicago-based trade house O'Connor and Co.

December surged over 75 percent of the 20-cent-per-bushel trading limit Wednesday and touched the highest level it had posted in about a month, with dwindling stocks of deliverable-grade wheat contributing to the advances.

The daily relative strength index (RSI) for the December closed at 63 points Thursday but had reached 70.7 points by the close of trade Wednesday. The 70-point level is considered overbought by many day-trading technicians.
In late dealings Thursday, SAK Futures sold two million bushels of March while Griffin Trading and FIMAT Futures each sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services bull spread two million bushels of December/March, sources said.
Wheat closed 1/4 to seven cents per bushel lower, with December down five at $4.08-1/4.
There were no changes in fundamentals with stocks of deliverable-grade wheat plus prospects for no wheat to be delivered on the CBOT December contract, underpinning the market.
Traders said the supply of wheat was in tight hands or held by commercial firms and was not likely to be delivered. First notice day for delivery on the December contract is slated for November 29.

Some pressure on the wheat market may have come from only routine exports with USDA Thursday revealing the U.S. net wheat export sales for the week ended November 14 at 275,100 tonnes. That tally was near the low end of trade expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
Traders said the EU's wheat rebate this week at just over 16.5 ECUs was neutral to the market.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 24,000 contracts, above the 23,438 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Paine Webber sold 200 March $3.60 puts at 3-3-1/4 cents, traders said. FIMAT Futures bought 400 March $3.90 calls and sold 400 July $3.60 calls at five cents.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 5,500 contracts, below the 5,680 traded Wednesday.
